MAP 1Tracer availability by district

How it is calculated: Method 1 - Expected medicines: available on the visit day / expected medicines, pooled over every facility in the district. Expected = for Essential Medicines, EML-authorised at the level (not managed counts as unavailable); for other programmes, managed only.

How it is calculated: Method 2 - Managed products only: available on the visit day / medicines the facility manages, pooled over every facility in the district. Every programme, Essential Medicines included, is on the managed base: a medicine the facility does not manage is left out, not counted unavailable.

FIG 7Unavailable at the facility - was the stock upstream? By level of care

How it is calculated: Unavailable rows answered 'Yes' at RMS Regional (or Central) / unavailable rows with a Yes or No answer for BOTH stores.

FIG 8Regional against Central, by programme

How it is calculated: Same base as FIG 7 - answered 'Yes' at the store / unavailable rows with a Yes or No answer for BOTH stores - by programme.

The same pairing by vertical programme. A programme where both bars are short is short at the national store itself.

FIG 9Distribution Gap against nationwide stock-out, by level of care

How it is calculated: Same base as FIG 7. Rows classed Distribution Gap (or nationwide stock-out) / unavailable rows with a Yes or No answer for BOTH stores, by level of care.

Distribution Gap: the medicine was not available at the facility but was available at RMS Central or RMS Regional level. Nationwide stock-out: not available at the facility, nor at RMS Regional or RMS Central.

FIG 10Distribution Gap against nationwide stock-out, by programme

How it is calculated: Same base as FIG 7. Rows classed Distribution Gap (or 'nationwide stock-out') / unavailable rows with a Yes or No answer for BOTH stores, by programme.

Distribution Gap: the medicine was not available at the facility but was available at RMS Central or RMS Regional level. Nationwide stock-out: not available at the facility, nor at RMS Regional or RMS Central.

Filter

FIG 2.1Stock adequacy overall

How it is calculated: Base = every stock-out (not on the shelf on the visit day). Under 1 = understock, 1-2 = adequate, over 2 = overstock (at teaching and referral hospitals 1-3 = adequate, over 3 = overstock).

FIG 2.2Stock adequacy mix by level of care

How it is calculated: As FIG 2.1 - stocked out, or months of stock classed under / adequate / over - shares within each level of care.

FIG 2.3Stock adequacy mix by programme

How it is calculated: As FIG 2.1 - stocked out, or months of stock classed under / adequate / over - shares within each programme.

Vertical programmes manage their own ordering, so the mix differs sharply between them.

FIG 2.4Stock adequacy mix by province

How it is calculated: As FIG 2.1 - stocked out, or months of stock classed under / adequate / over - shares within each province.

Most overstocked province first.

FIG 2.5Inventory record accuracy overall

How it is calculated: Left: records where physical count = system count / records with both counts that name a digital recording system. Right: mean over the same records of max(0, 1 - |system - physical| / system) x 100, with 0% where the system quantity is 0.

Left: physical count equals the system count. Right: quantity accuracy = (1 - |system - physical| / system) x 100 per record, 0% at worst and 0% where the system quantity is 0, averaged. Both across every record that names a digital recording system.

5.5Feedback and comments from data collectors

ThemeFacilitiesWhat was reported
Facilities that gave feedback109
RSSB reimbursement and medicine prices15Some medicines (beclomethasone spray, diclofenac suppository) are not reimbursed, so facilities avoid dispensing them; RSSB and RMS asked to harmonise prices and invoice verification.
Digitalise records and fully develop eBuzima13Health posts still keep paper records; parallel paper and system entry; MoH asked to add an offline module and link KWIVUZA / RSSB billing to eBuzima.
System downtime: prescriptions read from paper registers11eBuzima down, network or power cuts on the visit day, so prescriptions were taken from OPD registers or patient files.
System records disagree with stock or the prescription11Items shown out of stock in the system but dispensed; wrong quantities or strengths in eBuzima; stock reconciliation recommended.
Timely supply of medicines10Recommendation that RMS and partners make medicines available on time and in the right quantity.
Prescribing to stock hides unmet need9Prescribers write what the facility holds, so a medicine the patient had to buy outside cannot be seen - full service may overstate availability.
Stock-outs described9Specific medicines out on the day (insulin, salbutamol spray, lidocaine, thiamine), expired stock awaiting RMS delivery, part quantities dispensed.
Dosing and rational use6Paracetamol quantities that risk toxicity, age-appropriate forms for children, tapering doses, polypharmacy, under-dosing imposed for dental patients.
Enforce system use and refresher training2Staff have the system but do not use it fully; refresher training requested.
Referral and patient transfer2Ambulance delays at border health posts; nurses taken off duty to escort transfers.
